headline: LPG cylinders sell for Tk 3,500 in Bandarban, nearly double govt rate
summary: A severe shortage of liquefied petroleum gas has pushed prices up to Tk 3,500 for 12kg cylinders, far exceeding the government-fixed price of Tk 1,850.
details: In Bandarban town, 12kg LPG cylinders are being sold for between Tk 3,300 and Tk 3,500, despite the government-fixed price of Tk 1,850.
Many traders are reportedly refusing to exchange empty cylinders for refilled ones, forcing customers to purchase entirely new cylinders to get gas.
Some shops have remained closed with shutters down, yet cylinders are reportedly being sold from inside through phone arrangements.
The shortage has left many families unable to cook; one resident reported having to feed her young children bread because they had no gas.
Local dealers claim that supplies of major brands like Bashundhara are unavailable, leaving only a few specific brands available at inflated prices.
The Anti-Corruption Prevention Committee (Duprak) has alleged that trader syndicates are exploiting the shortage to artificially inflate prices.
Executive Magistrate Md Lutfur Rahman stated he was unaware of the price hikes but promised legal action if evidence of overpricing is found.
caption:

headline_marked: 3 scientists [[win Nobel medicine prize]] for optogenetics
headline: 3 scientists win Nobel medicine prize for optogenetics
summary: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann, and Georg Nagel are honored for discoveries that allow scientists to control nerve cells using light.
details: American Karl Deisseroth and Germans Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel have won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
They were selected for their groundbreaking discoveries concerning light-gated ion channels and optogenetics, which help researchers understand how the brain works.
Optogenetics allows scientists to switch the activity of individual nerve cells in a living brain on or off using light, a method now used in laboratories worldwide.
In clinical trials, this technology is being used to restore vision to people blinded by retinitis pigmentosa by inserting light-sensitive proteins into the retina.
Researchers also hope that optogenetics could lead to more precise cochlea implants, improving the stimulation of the auditory nerve compared to current electrical devices.
The three laureates will share a prize sum of 12 million Swedish crowns, approximately $1.2 million.
The discovery began in the 1990s when Hegemann studied how algae react to light, leading Nagel to discover channelrhodopsin-2, an ion channel that opens with light exposure.
By 2005, Deisseroth demonstrated the technique in rat nerve cells, and the method was officially named optogenetics a year later.
